summary: Mark Twain NF tower in Carter County; a 1934 paper placed its camp about 8 miles south of Fremont; CCC-built, 1970 heliport, 2008 refurbishing; standing; visitors can walk around it but not climb it.

facts.design: Four-legged steel structure with an enclosed observation room at the top (1962 NGS station description); quarters for the fire lookout crew (Forest Service)

access.note: The Forest Service says visitors can walk around the tower but cannot climb it or enter the buildings.

visit.trail_note: Near the Sinking Trailhead on the Ozark Trail; the Forest Service says parking at the trailhead is usually easy to find.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps; a May 17, 1934 report describes steel half up on one tower, foundations for a second nearly done, and both towers planned at 100 feet
May 17, 1934 report: quarters for the lookout to be built at each tower that summer (planned)
February 16, 1950 notice names the Sinking Creek lookout tower as the place to collect a strayed sow and three young pigs
A heliport was built near the tower in the 1970s; the helicopter was based there to be sent to fires on the Winona, Doniphan and Van Buren ranger districts (Van Buren Current Local, November 5, 1970)
October 2008 refurbishing of the lookout and associated structures under the Passport in Time program

notes_for_editor: Height is not in facts because the sources disagree: the 1934 report and the Forest Service both say 100 feet, while the 1962 NGS description says about 90 feet. Editor should decide which to show. The 1934 report describes two towers, but the sources describe only one standing tower and do not say what became of the second. Living New Deal page (livingnewdeal.org/sites/sinking-creek-fire-lookout-tower-briar-mo/) says the site is extant and not in active use; it was not cited because fetch_text got HTTP 403 and only a WebFetch summary was available. Worth adding if it can be cached. No staffing or fire history was found. The 1950 stray-sow notice is kept only as a dated mention of the tower. Brief agency and county confirmed. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the story no longer says the tower itself sits eight miles from Fremont; the source places the Sinking Creek camp there, so the story now says that. The 1950 notice covers a strayed sow and three young pigs, and the story says so.
